overview.summary: Many Nepali students begin in Japan at a Japanese language school, then move to a vocational school or university. Japanese ability shapes your study, work and career options, and the Embassy of Japan in Nepal warns applicants about brokers and false documents.
overview.educationSystem: Japanese language schools (1–2 years), specialised training colleges (senmon gakkō, usually 2 years), universities (4 years) and graduate schools. English-taught degrees exist mainly at graduate level and in some undergraduate programmes.

financialEvidence.requirement: There is no single published amount. Your school and the Immigration Services Agency assess whether you or your sponsor can pay tuition and living costs when they review your Certificate of Eligibility. The Embassy of Japan in Nepal warns that part-time income alone is not enough to cover tuition and living costs.

insurance.requirement: Students living in Japan join National Health Insurance.

conditions: You need “permission to engage in activity other than that permitted” before working.
Up to 28 hours per week; up to 8 hours a day during long school holidays.
Working in adult entertainment businesses is prohibited.
The embassy says the maximum earnings within legal hours are roughly ¥80,000–90,000 a month, which is not enough to cover tuition and living costs. Breaking work rules can lead to deportation.

lifestyle.text: School dormitories or shared apartments are common at first. Renting privately often needs a guarantor and key money.
Excellent trains; commuter passes reduce costs.
Hot, humid summers and cold winters in many regions; typhoons in late summer.
National Health Insurance covers 70% of most medical costs.
Very safe overall. Learn earthquake preparedness and follow rules on rubbish sorting and residence registration.
